pr_title: Implement Provider side SM2 Asymmetric Cipher support
pr_body:
This PR makes SM2 Asymmetric cipher support available via the default provider.

The work is essentially complete, but is marked as WIP because:

1) It is dependent on #12536 and #12884. The commits from both of those PRs are included here

2) There is an annoying doc-nits problem which I haven't yet solved

Fixes #12908
pr_comments:
> It looks like @mattcaswell spent less time adding the asymmetric support,
than the amount of time it took discussing if we should add it or not.

Quite probably
I rebased this and pulled in the latest version #12536. Also fixed the documentation issues identified by @levitte above.
Rebased on a fresh master now that #12536 has been merged. Now out of WIP. Please review!

> Please add a "Fixes #12908"

Add a squash commit to do that.

Fix ups for the various comments applied. Please take another look.
Travis red cross does not seem relevant.

> Travis red cross does not seem relevant.

Confirmed, they are timeouts.  I restarted those jobs just to see if we can get a full set of green, but that shouldn't stop a merge if the jobs aren't done before that
Oh. Oops. Looks like I inadvertently jumped the 24 hour grace period on this one (by just under 3 hours). Sorry! My mistake. :-(

issue_context.title: SM2 encryption in our providers
issue_context.body: SM2 encryption support in our providers is currently lacking, but does exist and work in legacy form.
comments: There's a vote going on whether we should simply drop SM2 encryption.

review_comments: why the _asym_ in the name? Are there likely to be more?
This name is used to disambiguate from the existing `sm2_encrypt` declared in include/crypto/sm2.h
not sure what the diff is on this file?
Only change in this file is to remove the extra blankline. The build issue which manifested here was resolved entirely in the build.info file.

propq needs to be passed here..
Which means it should be stored in the struct and be settable.

Does it? You can already provide properties and a digest name and they are settable. If you do then this code is never run because we already fetched the digest you specified using the properties you specified. This code kicks in where you haven't supplied an explicit digest name. So the only way we could get here and props be anything other than NULL is if you have not supplied an explicit digest name, but you did supply properties. I'm not sure that's a scenario we need to support??
(this is to my knowledge hypothetical) would you ever want to just set the fips property but not a digest name?
Not sure I understand what fips has to do with this issue? Which fips property do you mean?

It's possible I'm just confused, in which case sorry for the disruption.
But I thought that one of the uses of the propq was to be able to set `fips=yes` to require the fips property to be set for the fetched algorithm (which in practice will usually mean from our fips provider, but in theory could be a different one).
It did not stretch credulity to think that someone might want to restrict the fetched digest to being a fips-approved one without specifying exactly which one it has to be.  From just the context of this thread it seemed like that might trigger the case in question ("have not supplied an explicit digest name, but you did supply properties").

Right. The propq here should not be confused with the default propq that someone might use. So in order for this scenario to occur someone has explicitly sent a propq parameter to the sm2 asym cipher implementation, but not specified the digest. The assumption in this PR is that you must set both if you want the propq to be applied. So if you want to specify a specific propq then you must also specific a specific digest.
Thanks for the extra explanation, and sorry for my confusion.  I think I get it now.
There should be more of this sort that we can drop at this point...
... I mean, for other key types
Yes - that occurred to me too, but I thought it was outside the scope of this PR to address it.
Ah, yes, I didn't mean that it should be done in _this_ PR...  I just noted that it seems to be time to pull that plug.
Travis is having issues with the include here I think.
This was in the event of a no-ec or no-sm2 build. Down to a missing "$" sign in the build.info. Fixed now.
